prerequisites: Thorough knowledge of analysis (integrals and differentials for functions in multiple dimensions, ordinary and partial differential equations, Gauss and Stokes' theorems)
Thorough knowledge of analytical mechanics (Newton's laws)
Thorough knowledge of thermodynamics (equations of state, first and second laws of thermodynamics)

learning_outcomes.text: Students gain insight into the continuum description of the transport of mass, momentum, and energy in fluids and solids.
Students can derive transport equations in integral and differential form, starting from basic physical laws.
Students are also able to simplify the general transport equations into classical laws from fluid mechanics, heat transfer, and mass diffusion.

Within each of these disciplines, they have insight into physical models and empirical correlations for describing transport, and can formulate simplified equations for one-dimensional and two-dimensional systems that lead to analytical solutions.
Finally, students are able to solve simple problems related to applications in fluid mechanics, heat transfer, and mass transport.

syllabus_topics: Part I: General introduction to transport equations
Intro: Transport phenomena and examples from various disciplines within engineering sciences
Definition of a continuum and the continuum approach with focus on fluids
Properties of continua: state variables, viscosity, conductivity, surface tension, diffusion coefficient, …
Introduction to mathematical notation: scalar fields, vector fields and tensors (tensor notation, unit vectors and unit tensors)
Brief review of basic laws for closed systems for mass, momentum and angular momentum, energy
Reynolds transport theorem and integral formulations for general conservation equations
Reynolds transport theorem for conservation of mass, component mass, momentum, energy
Gauss divergence theorem: from integral formulations to differential forms and general closed set of differential equations for transport of mass, momentum and energy
Part II: Fluid mechanics
Hydrostatics
Kinematics of flows
Dynamics of flows
Dimensional analysis and Buckingham Pi theorem
Classification of flows: viscous/non-viscous; turbulent/laminar, compressible/incompressible
Non-viscous flows, Bernoulli's law, irrotational flows
Turbulent flows: the Reynolds-averaged equations
Internal viscous flows: channel flow, Hagen–Poiseuille and Couette flow, head losses in pipe systems
External viscous flows: boundary layers
Part III: Heat transfer
Storage & transport of heat
Dimensional analysis for heat transfer
Conduction, lumped-capacity solutions, convection (natural and forced, laminar boundary layers, Nusselt and Prandtl number, convection in pipes)
Radiation (Kirchoff's law, view factors, gray bodies)
Heat transfer processes in parallel and in series
Transient heat transfer
Applications: design of heat exchangers and cooling fins
Part IV: Mass transport
Simplified transport equations for mass
Velocity equation: Fick's Law
Dimensional analysis for mass transport
Analogy between heat and mass transfer (Reynolds analogy, Chilton-Colburn analogy)
Simplified cases and applications: unimolar diffusion, equimolar diffusion, transient diffusion in semi-infinite and finite media
